subject.title: fix(cli): install completion in effective shell startup profiles

question: Should OpenClaw accept an interactive Zsh `.zshenv` probe as the canonical way to discover shell-local, non-exported `ZDOTDIR` before writing completion configuration?
rationale: The proposed implementation fixes configuration roots that cannot be reliably learned from the parent process alone, but it deliberately executes part of the user's shell startup contract and therefore needs explicit owner acceptance of that runtime boundary.

options.title: Accept the canonical probe
options.body: Keep the bounded `.zshenv`-only probe and merge after refreshed checks confirm its timeout and no-side-effect boundaries.

options.title: Require a non-executing resolver
options.body: Reject startup-file execution and retain only environment-derived roots, accepting that shell-local reassignment is not covered.

recommendation.title: Accept the canonical probe
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded `.zshenv`-only probe and merge after refreshed checks confirm its timeout and no-side-effect boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review context identifies this contributor as the person with the most direct implementation knowledge of the completion-runtime change; final acceptance should still come through normal maintainer review.
